newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil plans concessions after Telebras selloff.
newsitem.headline: Brazil plans concessions after Telebras selloff.

text.p: - Brazil's Communications Minister Sergio Motta said Friday the government plans to offer concessions to interested competitors soon after federally owned telecom Telebras is broken up and privatized.
"That way we will have competition in every area immediately after privatization," Motta told reporters after a telecommunications forum here.

The government plans to break Telebras, which is comprised of 27 state-level operators and long-distance monopoly Embratel, into four regional holding companies and a long-distance firm and sell them off by the end of 1998.
First to be sold will be Telesp, the Telebras unit serving Sao Paulo, and long-distance monopoly Embratel, which will go on the auction block late this year or early next year, officials said.
The minister has said the government expects to rake in $35 billion from the privatization of telecommunications assets, including B Band cellular concessions.

Motta also said a cash-for-votes scandal that rocked Brazil's political circles and financial markets this week will not affect the privatization schedule for the telecom sector despite newspaper reports he may be involved.
"In terms of the government, this affects nothing," he said.
Motta has strongly denied he is involved in an alleged scheme to buy congressional votes in favor of a bill that will allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for re-election next year.
((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
